We constructed COCOLOFA, a dataset that contains 7,706 comments in the online comment sections of 648 news articles. Each comment is tagged for the presence of logical fallacies and, where applicable, the specific type of fallacy.
Table 4 shows the detection task results. BERT fine-tuned on COCOLOFA achieved the highest F1 score (0.86) on its test set...

We hired two experts from UpWork.com to assess the data quality. We specified that the experts should have abilities of identifying logical fallacies and writing the explanation to justify their annotations in our job description.
guideline: Experts rated each comment on a 5-point Likert scale for four questions: Q1 (grammatical correctness and fluency), Q2 (human-likeness), Q3 (confidence in annotation), Q4 (need for additional context).
Experts answered Likert-scale questions Q1–Q4 evaluating grammatical correctness, human‑likeness, confidence in annotation, and need for additional context.

We asked the experts to respond to the following questions for each comment using a 5-point Likert scale, from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree): (Q1) "Disregarding any logical fallacies, this comment is grammatically correct and fluently written." (Q2) "This comment appears to have been written by a person rather than by a language model such as ChatGPT." (Q3) "I feel confident about my annotation." (Q4) "I need some additional context to annotate the comment."
